The gate reads only the `'git', ['-C'` shape and exempts a whole file when the text gitEnv() appears anywhere in it (a comment counts). It misses git run in another directory through the cwd option (execFileSync('git', ['init'], { cwd: tmp }) inherits GIT_DIR just the same), execSync string commands, and backtick-quoted 'git'; and a second -C call without env added to wellknown.test.ts or git-env.test.ts would pass. Today no test hides behind this: the only cwd-form calls (tools/graph-check.test.ts:29, tools/feed-key.test.ts:142, tools/docs.test.ts:752, tools/ci.test.ts:168) are read-only and aimed at this repository. (tools/git-env.test.ts:25-31, found by the `unit` tier)

GIT_LOCATION omits the rest of git's own repository-local list (`git rev-parse --local-env-vars`): GIT_CONFIG, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, GIT_IMPLICIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_GRAFT_FILE, GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS, GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE, GIT_SHALLOW_FILE. None of these sends writes into another repository, but `git -c core.worktree=... push` exports GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS to the hook, and a temp repository would then add files from that work tree. GIT_NAMESPACE is in the list though git does not count it local; harmless. (apps/agent/src/service/wellknown.ts:63-72, found by the `unit` tier)
